Description: The global health major is a bachelor of arts degree and is designed to provide students an understanding of the complex determinants of health and disease in a global context. The major will provide students with the foundational knowledge needed to be a global health professional through an interdisciplinary curriculum with a strong focus in the social sciences. The curriculum focuses on five core global health concepts: 1) understanding the social and cultural determinants of health and disease; 2) learning about health-care systems and global health organizations and policies; 3) appreciating the role of history, politics, and economics in shaping health and disease patterns; 4) developing skills to critically analyze and assess global health inequalities; and 5) understanding the global burden of disease and demographic transitions. Students graduating with a global health major will develop skills in qualitative and quantitative research and communication and will gain in-depth knowledge of a particular global health topic through an upper-division concentration. The capstone of the major is a senior thesis or project that will allow students to integrate and apply the knowledge and skills they have gained in the major. Students who major in global health are well-prepared to enter a number of different fields, including graduate school in public health, medicine, or the social sciences; to work in government, nongovernmental organizations, or the private sector; or to serve in organizations such as the Peace Corps.

The bachelor of arts in global South studies provides a broad, interdisciplinary, and multicultural perspective on these global dynamics. The program of study is designed to offer a multifaceted and comparative perspective on the histories, political economies, cultures, and social formations of communities in Africa, Asia, and Latin America, as well as those of their diasporas. Students will work with faculty from across the arts and humanities and the social and natural sciences to examine key issues—including colonialism, slavery, migration, race, gender, sexuality, and indigeneity—as they have historically taken shape and as they have evolved to meet the political demands of the present. Description: The Human Developmental Sciences Program (HDS) offers a bachelor of arts (BA) and a bachelor of science (BS) and a minor. HDS is an interdisciplinary program that offers students a comprehensive understanding of human development from a variety of perspectives. Students learn about development from infancy and childhood through adolescence and aging. The program is organized around three thematic areas of development: biological development, cognitive and linguistic development, and sociocultural development. Students in HDS are encouraged to get involved in research and applied work to better understand development in a variety of real-world contexts. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the theories, research methods, and findings of developmental science. Students take courses in a variety of disciplines, including anthropology, biology, cognitive science, communication, education studies, ethnic studies, linguistics, psychology, and sociology. Through their course work, students learn to critically evaluate research and to understand the ways that biological, cognitive, linguistic, and sociocultural factors shape development across the life span. Upper-division courses allow students to focus on specific topics of interest, such as developmental neuroscience, language development, and the role of culture in development. The HDS major prepares students for careers in a variety of fields, including health care, education, social work, and law. It also provides excellent preparation for graduate study in a number of disciplines, including human development, psychology, sociology, and education. Graduates from the HDS Program have pursued advanced degrees in medicine, law, social work, counseling, clinical psychology, and education, and are employed in a variety of professional settings.

Description: The bachelor of arts in urban studies and planning is an interdisciplinary major that provides students with a variety of perspectives for understanding the development, problems, and policies of cities and urban areas. The curriculum for the major is designed to provide an understanding of the history and development of cities, the urban and regional planning process, the multicultural nature of American cities, and the role of social and economic factors in shaping urban environments. The program has five areas of concentration that enable students to focus on a particular area of interest. These areas of concentration are (1) urban/regional policy and planning, (2) city planning, (3) health, social, and environmental justice, (4) housing and community development, and (5) sustainability. Students select one of these areas of concentration around which to build a set of elective courses. All students must complete an internship in an urban-related organization and an advanced senior sequence project. In addition, the USP program offers students the opportunity to participate in a study abroad program. The major prepares undergraduates for a variety of careers in the public, private, and nonprofit sectors. It is also excellent preparation for graduate study in a number of fields, including urban planning, public policy, and law.
